# R4.5c — rustls admission (ADR-0365) + HTTPS/mTLS transport + `tls.terminate` honoured (DF-S2.4-2)

Spec: `docs/tickets/154c_R4.5c__rustls-tls-transport.md` (seq 154c).
Depends on R4.5b (one codec home, ADR-0364) + the 2026-10-20 operator ruling "Admit rustls (ring backend)".
Requirement ids: **DF-S2.4-2** (DONE 2026-10-21) · **BL-31** (TLS-transport leg discharged; row stays `open` — provider-adapter halves are R4.5d+) · **R-2.8.3**, **R-2.8.4** (`MET-ENGINEERED(DF-S2.4-2)` → `MET`) · **ADR-0266/0340/0341** (dated fired-answered notes) · **ADR-0359** (the `ring` provider this rides) · **ADR-0364** (one codec — TLS mounts beneath it) · **ADR-0365** (this admission) · the 2026-10-20 TLS ruling.

## Summary

The production TLS transport is landed under the operator's ruling. **ADR-0365**
(ADR-0359 pattern: exact `=` pins, crates.io publish dates recorded, ≥7-day
rule met — `rustls 0.23.46` at exactly 7 days, everything else well clear;
closed API scope; one named home) admits `rustls =0.23.46` on the
already-admitted `ring =0.17.14` backend — `default-features = false` +
`["ring","std","tls12"]`, no aws-lc, no `log` — plus `rustls-webpki =0.103.15`
and `webpki-roots =1.0.9` (`rustls-pki-types`/`zeroize`/`subtle`/`untrusted`/
`once_cell` as the named transitive set; `Cargo.lock` matches).

**`hh-tls`** (the 52nd member, the only crate that may name the graph):
`ClientTls` — webpki roots always verified (no insecure toggle anywhere;
`rustls-native-certs` deliberately not admitted — the OS trust store is never
consulted), extra roots only via an explicitly named PEM file (the local-CA
hook), mTLS client-certificate presentation (PKCS#8/PKCS#1/SEC1 keys);
`ServerTls`/`requiring_client_auth` for fixtures and the mediator;
`PeerIdentity` — verified peer subject-CN + DNS/IP-SAN extraction (the R4.7a
mediator's consume); `Read`/`Write` streams riding **beneath** the one
`hh_wire::http` codec — no second HTTP stack, `close_notify` on drop.

Consumers: `hh_wire::http` parses `http`/`https` (default ports, every
resolved address dialed); `hh-gateway` `HttpModelTransport::with_tls` mounts
`ClientTls` — `https:` legs ride real TLS, `tls_pending` is retired; `hh-embed`
`model_port` accepts `https:` + `tls{extra_roots_file,
client_cert_file+client_key_file}` (`env:` indirection; unpaired/unknown keys
and missing files are typed refusals at arm/drive); `hh-env`
`LocalTlsTransport` answers `terminates_tls()=true` — `tls.terminate` is
honoured with a real session, `tls_terminated` rows report truth, and a
non-terminating transport still refuses `tls_terminate_unsupported`;
`RevokeIntent.scheme` carries the destination's declared scheme so an `https`
revocation POST rides the TLS leg it revokes on (never silently plain).

## Test-only PKI

`scripts/gen-test-pki.sh` (openssl, ~100-yr expiry) →
`crates/hh-tls/fixtures/pki/` — CA, server (SAN `DNS:localhost`,
`IP:127.0.0.1`), wrong-SAN cert, client cert, rogue-CA cert. Committed
material is marked TEST-ONLY and allowlisted in `.gitleaks.toml`; these are
throwaway fixture keys, never credentials.

## Deviation — size budget

Measured **≈2,800 changed lines** (≈2,200 code+tests, excluding
`Cargo.lock`, the committed test-PKI fixtures, and generated
`docs/adr/README.md`) vs the 900 budget — surfaced, not silently exceeded:
the ticket is atomic (one admission ADR + its four consumers + the LT
battery can't subdivide without shipping dead surface mid-stack), and the
R4.5a/R4.5b recorded-Deviation precedent applies (orchestrator accept
pattern, per the appended ruling notes on those rows).
